messages:
Maya: throwing out a small ops UX idea: a lightweight "/pin-nudge" command for the deploy bot. intent: quickly move traffic back to a known-good revision with minimal handoffs. not a full rollback UI, just a safe nudge.

Rafi: love the premise. what are the must-haves?

Maya: musts: validation, dry-run preview, short TTL auto-revert, PR stub so the change is tracked, and an undo (/pin-unwind). bells: tmux helper for live triage and optional auto-merge rules.

Jordan: concrete command sketch: `/pin-nudge <svc> <rev> --reason "brief" --ttl 60 --dry-run`
- dry-run: show exact deployctl commands + PR diff
- ttl default 60m; bot will lift the pin after ttl unless `--hold` provided
- bot should refuse if the target revision is missing or if change-window policy forbids it

Priya: on the change-window check: require an explicit ack from the current oncall if inside the window, or two approvers otherwise. OpsBot can look up the calendar or a channel flag.

Nate: backend stub idea (for the bot team):
```
POST /internal/bot/pin-nudge
{ "service": "payments", "rev": "2026-03-21-abc", "reason": "regen payment spikes", "ttl_mins": 45, "dry_run": true }
```
Bot flow: validate registry -> produce PR diff -> post preview in thread -> wait for confirm -> apply pin -> start sentinel watch -> post summary.

Maya: sentinel watch = poll key signals for ttl window (cpu, error-rate, p95 latency, 5xx count). if anything breaches configured thresholds, bot posts a flagged status and suggests either revert or escalate.

Rafi: PR behavior: bot opens ops/rollpointer PR with a standardized template that includes: reason, incident link (optional `--note-url`), TTL, and the commands it ran. make the diff tiny and audit-friendly.

Priya: auto-merge rules: default = manual merge by oncall. allow opt-in auto-merge only when dry-run validated AND 15m quiet across signals AND 2 approvers. explicit opt-in flag `--auto-merge` required.

Jordan: UX in Slack: after `/pin-nudge --dry-run` bot should show a compact preview block with the PR patch, `deployctl` commands, a Confirm / Cancel button, and a small TTL selector. quick confirm should include an explicit checkbox: "I understand this will auto-unpin after TTL".

Maya: operator helper: tiny tmux script to watch logs/status during the TTL (for manual responders):
```
# scripts/tmux-nudge-watch.sh
svc=$1; rev=$2
tmux new -d -s nudge-$svc \\
  "stern -n 200 /var/log/$svc/*" \; splitw -v "watch -n 8 deployctl status $svc" \; splitw -h "watch -n 5 kubectl get pods -l app=$svc"
```
(we use stern if available, fallback to tail)

Nate: need endpoints in the bot for: validate-revision, create-pr, apply-pin, unpin, and metrics-query. prefer these behind a feature flag for a staging canary.

Rafi: also add a tiny audit table entry (db row) for every pin-nudge with fields: service, rev, initiator, reason, ttl, pr_url, status. OpsBot can post a compact audit row back to the thread when complete.

Priya: regarding rollback decisions later: if the sentinel suggests revert, bot should create a short poll (Yes: revert, No: keep) and require two maintainers to vote to revert; otherwise, escalate to oncall.

Maya: follow-ups and volunteers: Rafi + Nate will prototype the API + PR template. Priya will draft change-window logic and approval matrix. Jordan will mock the Slack interactive preview. I'll write a short RFC and PR template examples.

OpsBot: scheduled change window in 1h. Pin-nudge attempts during window will include a highlighted "requires oncall ack" badge.

Nate: I'll spin up a staging feature-flag branch and wire a dry-run endpoint this week.

Rafi: metrics thresholds to start with (TBD by Priya): p95 latency > 2x baseline, errors/sec > 5% above baseline, pod restarts > 3 in 10m. make them configurable per service.

Maya: summary: add /pin-nudge (dry-run preview, PR stub, TTL auto-unpin, undo command, sentinel for health signals, change-window checks, tmux helper). volunteers: Rafi, Nate, Priya, Jordan. aiming for staged canary in next sprint. :rocket:

Jordan: filing a placeholder GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/ops/issues/1234 (placeholder link)
